chunks: Ibn Faḍḍāl narrated from Ṣāliḥ ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Khathʿamī, who said:
I asked Abā ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام about a man who intends the fast, then his brother, who is upon his cause, meets him and asks him to break his fast. Should he break his fast?
He عليه السلام said: "If it is voluntary, it suffices him and it is counted for him; but if it is making up an obligatory fast, then he must make it up."

key_terms.أَخُوهُ: his brother, meaning a fellow believer
key_terms.عَلَى أَمْرِهِ: upon his cause or shared religious commitment
key_terms.قَضَاءَ: a compensatory fast performed to make up a missed obligation
key_terms.ٱلصَّوْمَ: the fast being intended or observed

ai.seo_question: If someone breaks a fast at a fellow believer’s request, does the fast still count?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about breaking a fast at the request of a fellow believer. It distinguishes between a voluntary fast, which is still counted for the person, and a make-up fast for an obligatory one, which must be performed again.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.2003 - Ibn Faddal narrated from Salih ibn Abd Allah al-Khath’ami, who said:
I asked Abu ‘Abd Allah (as) about a man who intends to fast and then meets his brother, who shares his faith, and his brother requests him to break his fast. Should he break his fast?
Imam (as) replied: "If it is a voluntary fast, it will suffice, and it will be counted for him. However, if it is a fast making up for an obligatory one, then he must make it up again."
